input.summary: The built-in `dark` theme (src/theme/dark.ts) declares a default `visualMap.inRange.color` ramp. Because component options are deep-merged with the theme (Component.ts `mergeDefaultAndTheme`), that ramp gets injected into every user-declared `visualMap` in dark mode, silently adding a color mapping the author never asked for (and suppressing the ec2-compat `visualMap.color` path). The fix is to delete the `inRange` block from the dark theme's `visualMap` section so dark mode only styles chrome (text/handle) and leaves visual mapping to the user's option / the global `gradientColor` default.
steps: PRE-CHECK (important): the change may already be present in the working tree depending on the round's baseline. Run `grep -n "visualMap" -A 12 /workspace/src/theme/dark.ts`. If the block already reads `textStyle` + a `// Do not provide \`inRange\` here.` comment + `handleStyle`, there is nothing to do — stop and report no-op. If it still contains an `inRange` key, apply step 2. (In the round-0 baseline commit the `inRange` block sits at src/theme/dark.ts lines 153-155, inside the `visualMap` object that spans lines 149-159.)

NO OTHER EDITS ARE REQUIRED. Verified: (a) no new public option is introduced — `inRange`/`outOfRange` are already typed in /workspace/src/component/visualMap/VisualMapModel.ts lines 95-106 (`VisualMapOption`) and need no change; (b) `VisualMapModel.defaultOption` (VisualMapModel.ts line 612 ff.) contains no `inRange`, so nothing else re-adds it; (c) the legacy standalone theme /workspace/theme/dark.js has a `visualMap` block (line 165) with only `textStyle` — it never had `inRange`, leave it alone; (d) no other theme/dark-mode code path injects `visualMap.inRange` (`grep -rn inRange src/` shows only heatmap/line/visualMap runtime code).

LINT SANITY: after deleting the two token references, confirm `color.neutral10` and `color.theme` are still used elsewhere in src/theme/dark.ts so no variable becomes unused — they are (`color.theme` at the top-level `color:` key and in `graph.color`; `color.neutral10` in `map.itemStyle.areaColor` and `geo.itemStyle.areaColor`). No import removal needed; `import tokens from '../visual/tokens'` stays.

UNDERSTAND/PRESERVE THE FALLBACK (no code change, just don't be tempted to add a replacement default): /workspace/src/component/visualMap/VisualMapModel.ts line 468 in `completeVisualOption`/`completeSingle` reads `base.inRange = base.inRange || {color: ecModel.get('gradientColor')};`. With the theme value gone, dark mode falls back to the global default `gradientColor: [lightThemeColor, themeColor]` (/workspace/src/model/globalDefault.ts lines 32-33 and 44), i.e. identical to light mode. Do NOT add a dark-specific `gradientColor` — the requirement is that dark mode stops supplying a mapping.

WHY THIS FIXES IT (for the commit message / review): /workspace/src/model/Component.ts line 170 does `zrUtil.merge(option, themeModel.get(this.mainType))`, a non-overwriting deep merge, so the theme's `inRange.color` was merged INTO a user object such as `inRange: {symbolSize: [10, 50]}`, adding an unrequested color ramp; it also made `base.inRange` truthy, which disables the ec2-compat branch at VisualMapModel.ts lines 454-460 that turns `visualMap.color` into `inRange.color`.

VERIFY: `cd /workspace && npx jest --config test/ut/jest.config.cjs test/ut/spec/component/visualMap` (existing specs live at /workspace/test/ut/spec/component/visualMap/setOption.test.ts and assert user `inRange` survives round-tripping through `getOption`), then `npm run lint` and `npm run checktype`. Manual check: open /workspace/test/theme.html or /workspace/test/theme-list.html with the dark theme and confirm a chart declaring its own `visualMap.inRange` keeps its colors.

OPTIONAL (only if the task asks for test coverage; the upstream-style patch is source-only): add a case to /workspace/test/ut/spec/component/visualMap/setOption.test.ts using `createChart({theme: 'dark'})` — /workspace/test/ut/core/utHelper.ts line 33-38 accepts a `theme` param — that sets `visualMap: {inRange: {symbolSize: [10, 50]}}` and asserts `chart.getOption().visualMap[0].inRange.color` equals the global `gradientColor` (import `globalDefault` as the file already does at line 27) rather than the dark ramp `['#e8ebf0', <theme[0]>]`.
